lines: מָה־אָשְׁרִי, מָה־אָשְׁרִי, כִּי שַׁדַּי הוּא אָבִי

review: The printed metre is 15.11.15.11 – 8.8.8.11: stanza 1 is the short fourfold acclamation and stanzas 2–4 carry the long lines. The payload follows that pattern, so the metre script's position medians (taken across all four stanzas) call stanza 1 short by design, exactly as with hymn 157.

1:3 חֶלְקִי כוֹסִי גוֹרָלִי — the Arabic قِسْمَتِي كَأْسِي نَصِيبِي keeps three words in apposition with no verb; the Hebrew keeps the same three (חֵלֶק, כּוֹס, גּוֹרָל), all of them nouns of Ps 16:5, rather than collapsing them into 'my portion'.

3:3–3:4 כְּיֶלֶד אֶל־אָבִיו … כִּי בְחֵיק אָבִיו יִשְׂבָּע — the Arabic مِثْلَ طِفْلٍ لِأَبِيهِ يَدْنُو لَا خَوْفَ لَهُ / بَلْ بِأَحْضَانِ أَبِيهِ يَشْبَع is that child-and-father image; the Hebrew keeps חֵיק ('bosom') and שָׂבַע ('be filled'), the verbs of Deut 33:23 and Ps 17:15.

4:3 וְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ בְּקִרְבִּי מַדְרִיכִי — the Arabic وَالرُّوحُ الْقُدُّوسُ فِيَّ مُرْشِدِي is 'the Holy Spirit in me is my guide'; the Hebrew uses the participial מַדְרִיכִי rather than a noun, so the line stays an active leading (Ps 25:5) and not a title.

2:3–2:4 לְמַעַן יִשְׁמַע שָׁמַיִם וָאֶרֶץ … מַלְאָכִים וּבְנֵי אָדָם יַחַד — the Arabic كَيْمَا تَسْمَعَ السَّمَا وَالْأَرْضُ تَرْنِيمِي لَهُ / الْمَلائِكَةُ وَالنَّاسُ مَعًا pairs creation with the two orders of praise; the Hebrew keeps the singular verb with the compound subject, as biblical Hebrew does (Ps 69:35).
